# C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns

*Level 1 card. 7 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly. This includes using slow iteration forms when faster alternatives exist (inefficient construct), recomputing values inside the loop that do not change across iterations (loop-invariant recomputation), performing expensive setup or allocation on every iteration (per-iteration setup), nested loops that could be flattened with better data structures (inefficient nesting), processing all items when only a subset is needed (unfiltered iteration), continuing past the point of usefulness (missing early exit), and modifying collections during iteration (array mutation).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | iterate the sequence directly, or express the loop as a comprehension | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | hoist the invariant expression to just above the loop | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | build it once before the loop and reuse it | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | replace the inner scan with a hash lookup, removing one loop level | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | break out, return, or use a short-circuiting builtin | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | narrow the input before doing the work, or stop once enough is produced | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | iterate a snapshot, or build the result and replace the collection | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C3.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S7.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C3.S1 vs C10.S1 Skipping Optimized Built-ins** — C3.S1 keeps the loop and changes how it iterates.  C10.S1 removes the loop entirely by calling a builtin that subsumes it.  Ask whether a `for` still exists after the repair.
- **C3.S1 vs C10.S3 Missing Bulk Primitive Usage** — C3.S1 replaces a loop with a comprehension (still Python-level looping). C10.S3 replaces it with a bulk primitive that loops in C (`list.extend`, `np.sum`).
- **C3.S2 vs C8.S3 Missing Local Lookup Caching** — C3.S2 hoists a *computation*.  C8.S3 hoists a pure *name or attribute resolution* with no computation attached.  `len(xs)` is C3.S2; `self.config.limit` is C8.S3.
- **C3.S3 vs C4.S6 Expensive Exception Control Flow** — C3.S3 is about per-iteration *setup* -- an object built each time round that could be built once.  C4.S6 is about exception handling used as control flow.  `try/except` inside a loop routes to both: if the repair hoists a construction out, it is C3.S3; if it replaces the exception with a test, it is C4.S6.
- **C3.S3 vs C8.S2 Missing Derived-Value Reuse** — Both hoist a compiled artefact; the difference is *how far*.  C3.S3 hoists to the enclosing function, fixing repetition within one call. C8.S2 hoists to module or class scope so the artefact survives across calls.  If the function is called once with a big loop, it is C3.S3; if it is called many times, C8.S2.
- **C3.S3 vs C6.S1 Unnecessary Object** — C3.S3's repair moves the construction (location changes).  C6.S1's repair eliminates or shares the object (count changes).
- **C3.S4 vs C7.S1 Suboptimal Algorithm Choice** — C3.S4 keeps the strategy and removes a loop level, usually by adding an index.  C7.S1 replaces the strategy with a *differently named* algorithm (bubble sort to Timsort, linear scan to binary search).
- **C3.S4 vs C5.S2 Missing Helper Type** — The two overlap heavily.  Pick C3.S4 when loop nesting depth drops.  Pick C5.S2 when the new index removes repeated scans but the loop structure is unchanged.
- **C3.S6 vs C6.S3 Unnecessary Data Materialization** — C3.S6 stops the iteration early because only part of the sequence is needed.  C6.S3 avoids materialising a sequence that is consumed lazily anyway.  `list(xs)[0]` is C3.S6 if the fix is `next(iter(xs))`; it is C6.S3 if the fix is to stop building the list while still consuming all of it.
- **C3.S6 vs C7.S4 Inefficient Operation Ordering** — C3.S6 reduces *how many items* are processed.  C7.S4 keeps the item count and swaps the *order* of two operations.  Filtering before sorting is C7.S4; taking only the top ten is C3.S6.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
